body:
When `endOfMonth` is set and the schedule is generated from an end-of-month seed, `Schedule` moves every inner date to the end of its month. This includes an explicit `firstDate` or `nextToLastDate`, so the stub that was asked for is silently changed. For example,

    Schedule s = MakeSchedule().from(Date(31, January, 2026))
                               .to(Date(15, December, 2027))
                               .withNextToLastDate(Date(15, November, 2027))
                               .withCalendar(NullCalendar())
                               .withTenor(6*Months)
                               .withConvention(Unadjusted)
                               .forwards()
                               .endOfMonth();

ends with July 31st, 2027, November 30th, 2027 and December 15th, 2027 instead of having the short final stub start on November 15th. Going backwards, a `firstDate` of February 15th, 2026 becomes February 28th. With a business-day convention the date can even move to the next month: a first date of February 27th, 2026 (the last TARGET business day of the month) is moved to the 28th and then rolled to March 2nd by `Following`.

The cause is the end-of-month pass at the end of the rule-based constructor, which applies `Date::endOfMonth` to all inner dates. The explicit stub dates are now only adjusted by the business-day convention, as #1509 already does for the effective and termination dates; regular dates are still moved to the end of the month.

The new test case `ScheduleTests/testStubDatesWithEomAdjustment` covers the three cases above. It fails on master with the dates quoted here and passes with the change; the other schedule tests and the full test suite pass.
